question: Will the Bank of Russia decrease the key rate after the July Meeting?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the change in the key rate resulting from the Bank of Russia’s July meeting, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting.

The resolution source for this market is information released by the Bank of Russia after its July 24, 2026 meeting as listed on the official Bank of Russia calendar: https://www.cbr.ru/eng/dkp/cal_mp/#t13

This market may resolve as soon as the Bank of Russia’s press release for their July 24, 2026 meeting with relevant data is issued. If no decision on the key rate is issued by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

evidence.excerpt: April–May saw a decrease not only in current price growth rates, but also in many measures of underlying inflation. For some participants in the discussion, that was sufficient evidence that inflation would continue decelerating under the influence of tight monetary policy. Others, however, argued that it would be premature to draw a firm conclusion about a further decline in underlying inflation measures, as they had been affected by strong, albeit transitory, disinflationary factors in recent months. The discussants agreed that proinflationary risks had increased, pushed up by both a stronger fiscal impulse and a temporary contraction in motor fuel production.

evidence.publisher: Bank of Russia — Governor Elvira Nabiullina
evidence.excerpt: I would like to emphasise that neither a further key rate cut nor the size of it is predetermined at any particular meeting. We might need to take pauses to analyse all incoming information and the effect of our earlier decisions.

The Russian central bank cut its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 14.25% on Friday, a smaller move than the 50 bps that analysts had expected, citing risks stemming from soft budget policy and a decline in fuel production. The economy contracted by 0.2% in the first quarter, and Nabiullina said it will grow by about 0.5% in the first half of the year.

Inflation in Russia accelerated to 0.87% in June 2026 after 0.17% in May, 0.14% in April, 0.60% in March, 0.73% in February and 1.62% in January, Rosstat said on Friday. The consensus forecast of economists surveyed by Interfax was 0.85% for the month. According to Rosstat, annual inflation accelerated to 6.02% in June 2026 (analysts expected 5.99%) from 5.31% at the end of May.
